question: What did the rulers of Vijayanagara call themselves?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Raya**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The rulers of the Vijayanagara Empire often used the title **Raya** to denote their sovereignty and authority.
 
• The term "Raya" signifies a king or monarch and was used as a suffix to the names of the emperors.
 
• Famous rulers like Krishnadevaraya and Devaraya I and II are well-known examples of Vijayanagara kings using this title.
 
• The title "Raya" emphasized the imperial power and the grandeur of the Vijayanagara rulers during their reign from the 14th to the 17th centuries.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Vijayanagara Empire:**

 
 
• The Vijayanagara Empire was established in 1336 by Harihara I and Bukka Raya I of the Sangama dynasty.
 
• It is renowned for its contributions to art, architecture, and the promotion of Hindu culture.
 
• Hampi, the capital city, is a UNESCO World Heritage Site, known for its rich architectural heritage.
 
 
 
• **Krishnadevaraya:**
 
 
• Krishnadevaraya (1509-1529) was one of the most illustrious rulers of the Vijayanagara Empire.
 
• He expanded the empire to its greatest extent and is known for his patronage of art and literature.
 
• His reign is often considered a golden age of Telugu and Kannada literature.
 
 
 
• **Devaraya I and II:**
 
 
• Devaraya I (1406-1422) and Devaraya II (1422-1446) were significant rulers known for their military and administrative prowess.
 
• They undertook extensive irrigation projects to boost agriculture and enhance the empire's economy.
 
• Devaraya II is also known for his contributions to temple architecture and the promotion of the arts.
 
 
 
• **Hampi:**
 
 
• Hampi was the capital city of the Vijayanagara Empire and is now a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
 
• The city is famous for its ruins, which include temples, palaces, and market streets, showcasing the empire's architectural brilliance.
 
• Prominent structures include the Virupaksha Temple and the Vittala Temple, known for their intricate carvings and grandeur.
